Rafaella Fontes

BackEngine MCP

Hey Hunters! We’re launching BackEngine MCP here today, and this is one of those products that pleasantly surprises me every day I use it (and I use it everyday).

Here’s why I think it matters.

Google made the world’s public information accessible to humans. That problem is largely solved. Anyone can find almost anything that was meant to be found.

BackEngine works on the opposite problem: making your company’s private knowledge safe and usable for AI.

That knowledge comes in two forms.

First, what your company knows: how you work, what you’ve built, the decisions you’ve made, and the context buried across your products and processes. [...] Second, the dynamic and constantly updating relational information such as what your customers have actually said (in their own words), across every call, ticket, email, and thread. This information exists nowhere else. It cannot be bought.

It belongs exclusively to your company.

Yet most businesses can barely access it themselves. It remains trapped inside the tools that collected it, invisible to the AI that could use it, and painfully manual for the people trying to make better decisions.

BackEngine exists to unlock that knowledge safely.

Our mission is simple: every piece of truth about a customer relationship should be instantly accessible to the person who needs it, at the moment they need it.

Today, we’re taking a major step toward that future with our MCP-first solution. [...] • And give leadership real visibility into account health  
All without adding more reporting or manual updates.

Review Thunai?

Reviewers consistently say Thunai is strongest at pulling scattered company knowledge into one searchable “brain” and using it to power fast, context-aware help across chats, calls, emails, meetings, and internal tasks. They often praise the human-like responses, clean summaries, easy setup, intuitive interface, and smooth integrations with tools like Slack, Zoom, Teams, CRMs, and email. Common use cases include customer support, onboarding, meeting notes, call summaries, and troubleshooting. The reviews are overwhelmingly positive, with no meaningful recurring complaints mentioned.

Liminary turns everything you’ve saved into working memory for AI. Unlike chatbots, meeting tools, or project-based notebooks, it gives your knowledge one shared memory across writing, meetings, and research. It surfaces relevant context automatically as you work, helping expert knowledge workers reuse their best thinking, avoid starting from scratch, and produce source-grounded work with traceable citations.

Free Options [...] Built for people who bill for their perspective: independent consultants, fractional leaders, VC analysts and strategists. In a world where everyone uses the same models, your edge is what those models are grounded in.

The work looks like this: you keep ambient context on a small set of clients, accounts, companies, or topics you think about repeatedly. You research them. You meet about them. results.content:

Review Lyzr?

Reviewers describe Lyzr as especially strong for privacy-sensitive AI work, saying its approach keeps data inside a company’s own environment and gives teams tighter control over the AI pipeline. They also like that it shows concrete use cases, such as document agents, interview tools, and other practical apps, which makes the platform easier to evaluate. Less technical users say it feels approachable, with a clear interface, reusable components, and helpful documentation, while another reviewer highlights fast business insights and useful analysis suggestions.
